meta.note: 4 reject / 3 accept at 0.30 -> clip verdicts are discriminative but thin (n=7).

experiment: Z4.02 sequential SPRT on calibrated log-odds
protocol: Wald SPRT over the clip's windows in time order. Per-window LLR increment, then cumulative S; stop reject if S>=A, accept if S<=-B, abstain if the clip is exhausted first. Primary mode='hard': binarise the calibrated ensemble bad-probability (1-p_ens) at 0.5, giving increments log(t1/t0) for a bad window and log((1-t1)/(1-t0)) for a good one (classic Wald SPRT). Secondary mode='soft': expected LLR from q=1-p_platt. Comparison mode='label': increments from the TRUE window labels (each processed window = one human review) = best case for a sequential review schedule. Clip error = 1 - agreement on decided clips; cost = mean windows processed (fraction of the clip).

best_cell_robustness.note: the decided/abstained partition is stable over this range, but the decide/abstain boundary sits between two clips' running extrema (desk min -3.69 vs ecu_late -3.92) -> fragile at n=7.

soft_mode_finding: the soft expected-LLR SPRT never reaches the accept bound on any clip: every clip's mean (1-p_platt) is positive, so good clips only abstain or (wrongly) drift to reject. The clip-level model probability is miscalibrated (a sign/offset shift, cf. the pallet inversion) -- binarising at 0.5 is what recovers the accept side. This is a calibration limitation, not a sequential-rule one.
review_savings_finding: Neither the deployable model SPRT (best tolerated cell 66.5% of windows) nor the label-oracle SPRT (65.5% at 7/7) processes fewer windows than the fixed every-2 grid (51.5% at 7/7). Sequential early-stopping does NOT drop review at equal clip error on these clips: because the bad rate climbs with time (E3: 0.09 sec1 -> 0.58 sec5), an early stop is biased good and must wait for the tail. This confirms E3's preference for a fixed time-spread grid.
recommendation: Keep the fixed every-2 grid as the sampler. Use the SPRT only as a clip-level ABSTAIN gate: decide by threshold, and if the cumulative evidence is still inside the bounds at the end, send the clip to a human. The best tolerated cell shows the mechanism (5/5 correct, 2/7 abstained) but is not cheaper.
caveat: 7 clips; the frontier is a coarse staircase and the best cell's accept bound separates desk (running min -3.69) from ecu_late (-3.92) -- a 1-clip-wide margin. Treat the cell as illustrative, not deployable. abstain = send the clip to a human.
